findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).
findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.

findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute
findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.

findings.evidence: In project-settings, a Save button in the form has no specified target or action, and the artifact shows no feedback state or success screen. In invite-member, a Save button similarly has no target, with a separate Continue link following it. In notification-settings, a Save button has no target or feedback state specified.
findings.fix: For each form's Save button, specify a feedback state: either inline success confirmation text, a loading indicator while processing, or a target screen the user is directed to upon success.

instances.location: the "project-settings" section, the Save button in the project name form
the "invite-member" section, the Save button in the email form
the "notification-settings" section, the Save button in the settings form

findings.location: the "project-settings" section, the Save button in the project name form
findings.violation: Save actions that change state do not specify what the user sees while saving or after it completes, leaving the user uncertain whether the action succeeded.

findings.evidence: invite-member section has a Cancel link returning to project-settings, but the artifact never specifies whether the email address entered in the form is discarded or preserved.
findings.fix: Add text to the artifact stating the result of cancellation, for example: "Unsaved changes will be discarded." or "Your draft invitation will be saved."
findings.violation: The exit control does not specify what becomes of the work already entered (the email address), leaving the user uncertain about the cost of exiting.

findings.evidence: workspace-overview section contains "Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on" in a promo-referral div, appearing among the primary content elements (recent projects list and control links).
findings.fix: Move the promotional content below the projects list, or visually separate it with reduced prominence so the primary action (viewing projects) is not delayed by secondary messaging.
findings.violation: Secondary promotional content is placed with equal weight to the primary task (viewing projects), competing for the user's attention and delaying access to the main function.

findings.evidence: notification-settings section uses "Digest frequency" as a label for a select control, but provides no tooltip, hint, or explanatory text. The term is not defined anywhere in the artifact.
findings.fix: Add a tooltip, help icon, or hint text next to the Digest frequency control explaining what it means, for example: "How often you receive email summaries of notifications."
findings.violation: A control whose label uses terminology not defined elsewhere in the artifact offers no in-place explanation, leaving the user without guidance at the point where they need it.
